## papers 3.0.0b6

Fixes found by writing a specification of papers for other programs
(`design/`, for a Rust implementation and Papers Desktop), and:

- **History steps are named by a hash of the state**, as git names its
  commits: `papers history` shows `4f1c9a2e papers add ...`, and
  `papers restore`, `papers history --revert` and `--drop-files` take any
  start of it, 4 characters or more. Step numbers could be given again
  after the history dropped its oldest steps. The history of earlier
  versions is converted at the first command, and nothing else changes.
- **The origin copies name a pool by its library identifier**, not by its
  path: a library moved away from its pool (then `papers config pool
  NEWPATH`) keeps its exchange records. Before, the pool's corrections
  were silently not pulled.
- **`papers file fix` also looks in the history**: a file that a papers
  command deleted from the place of a broken link comes back there.
- **A setting given to a library is saved, even with the default value**:
  `papers init` really stores `paths`, so a library keeps its link style
  on another computer. `papers config --unset NAME` makes a setting follow
  the global configuration again.
- **Paths typed on the command line are relative to the current
  folder**, as for any command: `papers init lib --pool ../pool` and
  `--bibtex`, `--filesdir` now read them from where you are (before,
  `--pool` was read from the new library). How they are stored doesn't
  change.
- **All of `.papers/` is in the library folder**, also when the bibtex is
  in a subfolder: `distinct.json` and `origin/` were next to the bibtex.
  They are moved the first time the library is opened.
- **A wrong value in `config.json` is an error** that names the file and
  the setting (`"auto-push": "no"` counted as true). A global
  configuration that is not valid JSON is an error too; before, it was
  ignored, and the next `papers config --global` overwrote it. Keys papers
  doesn't know are kept when it saves the file.
- **The history keeps to its size**: with a small `history-size`, deleted
  files beyond it dropped every step but the last, and the files stayed
  for an hour. Now the oldest steps go first, with their files.
- Undo and redo with a pool that changed since: redo does the pool's step
  again there; the files that the pool's revert placed are part of its
  step; an auto-push after undo that sends something is a new step.

Fixes:

- Two entries whose files get the same name: the second file gets a `-2`
  suffix. Before, papers asked whether to replace the file: yes overwrote
  the other entry's PDF for good, no linked the entry to it.
- The lock: two commands waiting on the same stale lock could both take
  it; a refresh could overwrite the lock of another command.
- `push` added back a file link that the pool had removed (shallow
  library), and `papers status` said `both changed`.
- The bibtex is read and written as UTF-8 with LF line endings on every
  platform (it followed the locale on Windows); a byte order mark is
  dropped instead of moving into the file; a block that papers cannot read
  no longer grows by a line at each save.
- `papers check --auto-key` renamed a key that was already right
  (`smith2000` became `smith2000b`).
- A merge wrote `month = jan` as `{jan}`.
- Names in braces are one word: `John {van der Berg}`, and organisations
  (`{Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change}`) for keys.
- BibJSON: a bibtex field `type` (of a techreport) or `id` overwrote the
  entry type or key; it is now written as `bibtex:type` (BibJSON namespaced
  keys) and read back.
- RIS: a blank line after `TY` stopped `papers add` (`error: 'title'`, a
  bug of rispy, reported); the DOI of a doi.org link next to another URL
  was lost.
- Undo brings back a file that a command deleted while its link stayed.
- The file operations done after a save that recorded no step joined the
  step of the previous command.
- A library can't be its own pool: `papers config pool .` is refused, as
  `init --pool .` was. A configured pool that has a pool of its own is an
  error for pull, push and sync.
- `papers list --porcelain` writes the listing on standard output.
- Tag add, remove and rename ignore case, as `--tag` does:
  `papers tag --rename climate ocean` also renames `Climate/Arctic`.
- Two keys that differ only by case, or two fields of an entry that do: the
  second is reported as unreadable and kept as text, as for a key given
  twice.
- File names that papers makes avoid the characters Windows refuses and
  are cut at 250 bytes, keeping the extension; `{journal}` of an entry
  without journal is empty (it was `None`).
- RIS and CSL-JSON import: `&`, `%`, `#` and `_` are escaped for LaTeX
  (not in URLs, DOIs or keywords); a last RIS record without `ER` is read;
  `urldate` and `translator` go to RIS (`Y2`, `A4`) and back; a container
  title is the `journal` except for chapters and conference papers;
  `edit --from FILE` reads file links from FILE's folder, as `add` does.
  All exports are written with LF line endings.
- `papers status` writes nothing in the library; it sees a change of entry
  type, an entry removed from the pool, and links that pull would repair.
- Pull and push: a case or brace fix (`{CO2}`) made on one side is sent;
  a pool key reused for another paper is no longer taken for the same
  paper; an entry renamed onto a removed entry's key no longer takes over
  its record.
- A merge no longer adds empty fields; key letters go on after `z`
  (`smith2000za`); `--keep-old-key` no longer repeats a key in `ids`.
- `and` or a comma inside braces in author names is handled the same way
  everywhere (keys, file names, duplicates).
- Absolute links in a library with relative paths become relative at the
  next save.
- `papers history --bibtex FILE` works without a library; `--remove` and
  `history-size 0` free the files no step needs; a command that saved the
  pool several times is undone in full; `file fix` copies from the history
  are kept as long as their step.
- The lock without hard links (some network drives) could lose a fresh
  lock during a takeover.
